title: A Congress for Europe’s Future
gist: Janis A. Emmanouilidis welcomes Ursula von der Leyen's proposal for a new Congress of Europe in 2027, modeled on the 1948 Congress and timed to the Treaty of Rome's 70th anniversary, as a step in the right direction given Europe's geopolitical challenges, but warns it must fix the shortcomings of past similar exercises.

themes.theme: Von der Leyen's Congress of Europe

insights.claim: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed in her State of the Union address to convene a new Congress of Europe next year, coinciding with the 70th anniversary of the Treaty of Rome.
insights.speaker: JANIS A. EMMANOUILIDIS
insights.so_what: A 2027 calendar marker for EU institutional-reform debate that could shape integration, defense and fiscal agendas.
insights.locator: In her latest State of the Union address

insights.claim: The proposed Congress is modeled on the 1948 Congress of Europe, which gathered political leaders, intellectuals and civil-society representatives to debate how a devastated continent could build a peaceful future.
insights.speaker: JANIS A. EMMANOUILIDIS
insights.so_what: Signals ambition for a foundational, broad-participation rethink of the EU rather than a narrow treaty tweak.
insights.locator: In her latest State of the Union address

insights.claim: Given the scale of Europe's geopolitical challenges, a new Congress of Europe is a step in the right direction, but it will only succeed if it addresses the shortcomings that hampered similar past efforts.
insights.speaker: JANIS A. EMMANOUILIDIS
insights.so_what: Temper expectations: EU citizen-engagement/reform exercises have a history of underdelivering; watch whether outcomes feed into binding decisions.
insights.quote: to succeed, it must address the shortcomings that have hampered similar efforts in the past
